payload.name: Preserve all components of stated symbolic meanings
payload.description: When a speaker explains what something symbolizes, stands for, or means and lists multiple aspects, preserve every listed component during extraction.
content: During candidate extraction, if the source text describes what something symbolizes, stands for, or represents and mentions multiple components, keep every explicitly stated component in the candidate content.
Do not replace a specific listed component (activity, context, or purpose) with a broader paraphrase that drops it; include the full set of meanings exactly as stated.

solves: During construction extraction, candidates may paraphrase a multi-part symbolic meaning and drop one explicitly stated component, leaving memory incomplete and future answers wrong. This skill is a reusable extraction rule: when source text defines what something symbolizes, stands for, or means, preserve all listed components rather than summarizing them away. It applies to any future statement that explains the meaning or representation of an object, phrase, tattoo, logo, or action.
